@CorneJB Since it is only the timestamp, and not the author name/email itself that is incorrect, the only place in the pipeline I imagine this affects is the division of time slices using the commit timestamp instead of the author timestamp. So you can actually check that yourself: Subtract the author timestamp from the committer timestamp on your dataset, and check if the difference is less than the size of the time window you chose for the slices (the default was 3 months in the Notebook). From memory, I don't think anything else would get affected (since all metrics are computed after a slice is created). 

In layman terms: If the time between the author submission (e.g. pull request or patch) is less than 3 months (or another time window you chose), then the slices should be the same, and consequently, I'd expect all the results to be the same. 

The interesting thing is that, despite being an oversight on my part on that line of code, the theory behind it is not necessarily "a bug" or "noise" I think: Yes, you are assessing the network of author file changes from git log, and comparing it with when the authors possibly shared e-mail threads (e.g. radio silence metric)  on the mailing list --but-- you opted to assume discussion would happen **during the time of commit** instead of the **the time of the patch/pull request**. If you consider pull request and patches can sit around for a while until a reviewer come by and a discussion occurs, maybe this mistake can even be more accurate as an assumption. Conversely, you could argue discussion would happen closer to when the author would be trying to make the patch...or maybe both! :^) Hope this gives you some food for thought! (pinging @harismumtaz18 @tuejari since this may be of interest to them). Maybe @maelstromdat or @rnkazman have another interpretation of this too.

But by all means, don't take my word for it, do give some thinking based on the code and the implications! This is one reason why I decided to follow the "Here's a notebook so you see the analysis steps and intermediate data", rather than "here is a command-line you run and whatever output you get take my word for it!" 😅

I had a similar problem, but the workaround did not work for me. 
I replaced the `as.POSIXct` functions with `stringi`'s `stri_datetime_parse` functions https://rdrr.io/cran/stringi/man/stri_datetime_format.html and that solved it for me.

So for example, in `social_smells_showcase.Rmd` I replaced lines:

```
project_git$author_datetimetz <- as.POSIXct(project_git$author_datetimetz,
                                              format = "%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y %z", tz = "UTC")
project_git$committer_datetimetz <- as.POSIXct(project_git$committer_datetimetz,
                                              format = "%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y %z", tz = "UTC")
project_mbox$reply_datetimetz <- as.POSIXct(project_mbox$reply_datetimetz,
                                        format = "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S %z", tz = "UTC")
```

with 

```
project_git$author_datetimetz <- stringi::stri_datetime_parse(project_git$author_datetimetz,
                                              format = "E MMM d HH:mm:ss yyyy Z", 
                                              lenient = FALSE,
                                              tz = "UTC", 
                                              locale = NULL)
project_git$committer_datetimetz <- stringi::stri_datetime_parse(project_git$committer_datetimetz,
                                              format = "E MMM d HH:mm:ss yyyy Z", 
                                              lenient = FALSE,
                                              tz = "UTC", 
                                              locale = NULL)
project_mbox$reply_datetimetz <- stringi::stri_datetime_parse(project_mbox$reply_datetimetz,
                                              format = "E, d MMM yyyy HH:mm:ss Z", 
                                              lenient = FALSE,
                                              tz = "UTC", 
                                              locale = NULL)
```

The code snipets you refer above:

```r
i_commit_hash <- data.table::first(project_git_slice)$commit_hash 
j_commit_hash <- data.table::last(project_git_slice)$commit_hash 
```

Are applied to project git slice, not project git (note this happens after the code snippet to date conversion). The process conceptually should go like this:

## 1) First the slices are identified in an array of slices on the `time_window` variable:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/65a99b40304af16d07470be8e9eac6b221251ceb/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L196-L208

`start_commit` and `end_commit` , which in turn are defined by the user on the project configuration file:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/65a99b40304af16d07470be8e9eac6b221251ceb/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L69-L70

So the range of time windows should be correct. 

## 2) The question then is whether the rows that go into each slice (which subsequently will be used to compute the metrics) is correct:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/65a99b40304af16d07470be8e9eac6b221251ceb/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L246-L262

Lines 246-256 are in charge of that, not 261 and 262. Lines 246-256 define the content of `project_git_slice` and `project_mbox_slice`. Since this is a boolean operator over the already converted timestamp, and not based on order, I would believe this to be correctly assigning the right rows to the right slices. However, the `first_commit` and the `last_commit` of said time slices are likely incorrect, since they are based on the position of the table. 

## 3) So if we agree the content that goes in each time slice is correct, but the first and last commit hashes can be wrong for depending on sorting, then the concern is when the slice is put together:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/65a99b40304af16d07470be8e9eac6b221251ceb/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L336-L352

The `commit_interval` is potentially incorrect due to the issue you noted, as it is a simple concatenation of `i_commit_hash` and `j_commit_hash`. However, `start_day` and `end_day` are obtained from the vector of slices I noted before, which should be correct:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/65a99b40304af16d07470be8e9eac6b221251ceb/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L241-L243

## 4) Finally, another point of concern that came to mind is whether these commits are used to align the data from various sources (e.g. Line Metrics with Social Smell Metrics):

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/65a99b40304af16d07470be8e9eac6b221251ceb/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L498-L504

This is done by `commit_interval`, which is the variable of concern. This one is interesting since it is an inner join, so if there were inconsistencies with i_commit_hash and j_commit_hash for example, we would have caught much sooner entire time windows were just missing or the table would be empty. But I don't recollect any occurrence of that insofar. My guess is that since the subsetting code is, in essence, the same across Line Metrics section, Social Smell section etc (they could in fact be a single giant loop but readability suffers in the Notebook), I'm assuming the issue you raised affects all these loops systematically. 

In other words, the potentially incorrect i_commit_hash and j_commit_hash, if they are reported wrong for a time window in Social Smells, it will also consistently be incorrectly put for the Line Metrics. End result, the join will still be done "correctly" thanks to the consistency, even though the hash value itself **mismatches to the start_date and end_date**. 

## 5) TL;DR:

I'd expect the final result table to be correct, including the "start_date" and "end_date" reported in the table, but the `commit_interval` to be potentially incorrect (as it is subject to the order as you reported).

Yes, thanks for replacing to slice and using first(), this should be ok since the return of multiple rows occurs when the commit has more than one file (on my quick test I guess I got a commit of a single file).

Concerning `Lines`, `Code`, `Comments`, `Blanks`, and `Complexity`, in retrospect, this makes sense to have discrepancies. I skipped to merge when checking, but I neglected to consider this:

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/65a99b40304af16d07470be8e9eac6b221251ceb/vignettes/social_smell_showcase.Rmd#L464

For some tools we use, analysis has to be done based on "what is in the folder in a specified filepath". Kaiaulu works around that by performing `git_checkout()` over a commit hash. In which case, as shown above, `j_commit_hash` is used. Therefore...if there was a misalignment between the dates being used and commit hashes, which you verified in raising this issue, then the line metrics above are incorrectly associated to a different time window (that of the incorrect commit range). 

So yes, the analysis is therefore compromised for those metrics as the data you show reflects. This should also be the case on the social-smell branch, but not the case on any analysis done before the https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/commit/4b844cc8c978a51f23dae540e3400847db998eb7.  

With that being said... I am not certain why `org_silo` and `missing_links` are being affected by it, as the git checkout workaround is not used on them (since Kaiaulu does not defer analysis to a 3rd party tool requiring the workaround). Neither uses the clustering algorithm either, and I believe I seeded it for reproducibility anyway.
